original_text: The modern concept of ideal weight began with the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company in the 1940s. MetLife analyzed mortality data from millions of policyholders and published "desirable weight" tables based on height and frame size. These tables defined the weight range associated with the lowest mortality risk. While groundbreaking for their time, they were based almost entirely on white, middle-class Americans who could afford life insurance, introducing significant demographic bias.
